findings.NATIVE-EFB-02: Resolved per-file native identity/namespace boundary: retain Windows locked ancestry and read/delete file handle; hash/delete exact open identity without write/delete sharing. POSIX anchored directory descriptors and private no-replace atomic claim; verify actual inode/content, restore changed claim without replacing new name, preserve any un-restorable claim and report refusal. Manifest anchor removed last; unowned/modified directories preserved.

scope_limits: POSIX binds filesystem identity and namespace; it does not claim atomic byte compare-and-delete against arbitrary writes through already-open external descriptors.
Multi-file uninstall is not an atomic co-commit. A refusal can follow previously settled removals; remaining anchor and changed/unowned state are preserved.
Focused tests use explicitly synthetic program payloads and real host filesystem APIs, not installed shipping artifacts, protected provider admission or Desktop/E2E.
